Subject: VertexSys — inference fit recap, Redwood-verified profiles & pilot next steps

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today, Daniel — good conversation on the latency/cost targets and the instruction-following edge cases. Summarizing the key points + the recommended next steps so we have a single action plan.

Recap (short)
- Primary workload: customer-facing generative assistants (single-turn, ~20–40 tokens output typical) plus a small reranking path for suggestions.
- Target SLO: p95 generation latency ≤ 220 ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens), sustained throughput target of ~120 TPS during peak bursts.
- Quality sensitivity: control over hallucination on product descriptions; recent internal prompts show occasional regression when we push quantized checkpoints.

Redwood recommendations (model + perf profiles)
- Recommended primary candidate: redwood-inference-13b-q4_0 (8-bit quantized, production profile). Verified p50/p95 at our standard 32-token session: p50=48ms, p95=210ms on our us-west dGPU pool.
- Cost-friendly fallback: redwood-inference-7b-q4_0 (excellent latency/cost balance for the bulk of queries).
- For the reranker path: use an embedding-based bi-encoder + small 3B cross-encoder for final scoring.

Why these choices
- Verified profiles: the attached rdw_verified_profiles.csv contains the Redwood-verified TPS/latency percentiles we measured with your approximate request mix. It includes the sequence-length distribution we discussed and KV-cache assumptions.

Benchmarks & artifacts (attached / links)
- vertex_perf_report.pdf — end-to-end benchmark with your sample prompt set (attached).
- vertex_prompt_pack_v1.json — the prompt set we used for the baseline runs (attached).
- Perf profiles: https://console.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/vertexsys-202610 (interactive view).
- Full benchmark results: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/vertexsys-20261018

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Pilot kickoff: 2-week pilot with the 13B quantized candidate behind a dedicated route so we can gather production-esque metrics (latency percentiles + token costs).
2) Provide a baseline regression suite: please confirm if the attached prompt pack represents the critical cases — we'll add a 2–3x adversarial set if you want.
3) Pilot config asks: target TPS concurrency, expected daily QPS, and any regulatory constraints (we'll need to enable stricter retention on logs for compliance).

Ask to you
- Can you confirm the peak TPS target (we noted ~120 TPS) and whether the p95 <= 220 ms is a hard SLO for launch?
- Any preference for model-family (we can surface a Llama2-variant if you prefer non-Redwood weights).

I'll loop Marcus and Dev on the pilot sizing and a draft credit/price for the 2-week evaluation. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite for a pilot kickoff tomorrow or Tuesday.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Stephanie — this is great context and I appreciate the clear options. A couple quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Latency percentiles: the p95 numbers in rdw_verified_profiles.csv look promising, but can you confirm the workload config used for those numbers (batching policy, concurrency, GPU type)? We run GPON-like bursts and need to understand how predictive the profile will be under our tail behavior.

2) Quality regression: we've seen that some quantized checkpoints drift on instruction-following tasks (especially multi-step product-compose prompts). I attached a short sample prompt pack with edge-cases — please run that against the recommended models and flag any regressions. If regression is non-trivial, we may need a tuned instruction-finetune or to pin a full-precision variant for the reranker path.

3) Throughput targets: 120 TPS peak is what we modeled — that's a hard requirement for peak windows; average QPS will be lower. For the pilot, we want to test a 2-hour window at peak load to see real tail behavior.

If you can confirm the pilot config (GPU type, expected concurrency, and targeted p95) I can book the internal ops window.

Daniel
Daniel Cho | Director, Platform Engineering
Vertex Systems
daniel@vertexsys.com | (617) 555-0136

Attachment: vertex_sample_edge_prompts.json (sample)

Stephanie / team — looping in sizing and pricing notes for the 2-week pilot. Summary and proposed config: 

Pilot config (proposed)- Model: redwood-inference-13b-q4_0 (primary); redwood-inference-7b-q4_0 (fallback route)
- Hardware: 1x T4s-equivalent accelerated pool for warmups + autoscale to 3x during the 2-hour peak window (we can pin GPUs for dedicated pilot windows)
- Batching policy: adaptive batching with max_batch_size=64, latency SLO target p95<=220 ms (we'll enforce request prioritization for short requests)
- KV/prefix cache: enabled for the repeated prompt fragments you showed (saves ~25% token work)

Metrics we'll collect- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU util, token-in/token-out counts, cache hit-rate, and quality regression flags against your provided prompt packs.

Pricing & pilot credits- Proposed: complimentary evaluation credits to cover the two-week run up to 150k tokens, then standard evaluation rate for excess. If you want a guaranteed reserved window (pin 3 GPUs for the 2-hour peak) we can provide a short-term discounted commit — I'll pass exact numbers once Stephanie confirms the likely peak hours.

Compliance & docs- We'll include SOC2 attestation and an export of the audit log for the pilot window on request. Stephanie: please confirm whether Vertex needs a redacted data retention policy during the pilot (we can enable strict retention and no-log for queries flagged as PII).

Action items (internal)
- Steph: propose kickoff slots to Daniel (tomorrow or Tue).
- Dev: prepare the pilot environment (+ pin GPUs if customer wants guaranteed window) and pre-load the prompt set.
- Marcus: draft the short pilot credit/price note to attach to the kickoff email.

LMK and I'll take the lead on the pilot economics note.
